sections.heading: 1. Present Passive Voice — form
sections.content: Greek verbs have a passive voice in the present tense formed by replacing the active endings with passive endings. The key marker is the mediopassive ending: -ομαι / -εται / -ονται (instead of -ω / -ει / -ουσι). The passive expresses that the subject receives the action rather than performs it.

table.caption: Present passive — λύω (to loose → to be loosed)

examples.greek: τὸ πνεῦμα δίδοται ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ
examples.note: the Spirit is given by God (3rd sg. passive; ὑπό + gen. = agent)

noteTranslations.es: el Espíritu es dado por Dios
noteTranslations.fil: ang Espiritu ay ibinibigay ng Diyos

examples.note: it is sent by the Father (3rd sg. passive)

noteTranslations.es: es enviado por el Padre
noteTranslations.fil: isinusugo ng Ama

examples.note: he is saved by God

noteTranslations.es: es salvado por Dios
noteTranslations.fil: nailigtas ng Diyos

examples.note: he is scorched by the sun

noteTranslations.es: es abrasado por el sol
noteTranslations.fil: naiinitan ng araw

sections.heading: 2. Agent with Passive — ὑπό + genitive
sections.content: When a passive verb names the agent (the one performing the action), Greek uses ὑπό + genitive. This is the standard way to express 'by someone' with a passive verb. Compare: ἐν + dative expresses location, not agency.

examples.note: they are forgiven by God

noteTranslations.es: son perdonados por Dios
noteTranslations.fil: pinapatawad ng Diyos

examples.note: he is taught by the Spirit

noteTranslations.es: es enseñado por el Espíritu
noteTranslations.fil: itinuturo ng Espiritu

sections.heading: 3. δεῖ + Infinitive — 'it is necessary'
sections.content: δεῖ (impersonal verb, 'it is necessary') is always followed by the accusative + infinitive: the person required to act is in the accusative, and the action is the infinitive. δεῖ itself never changes form.

examples.note: it is necessary for the person to repent (acc. + inf.)

noteTranslations.es: es necesario que la persona se arrepienta
noteTranslations.fil: kailangang magsisi ang tao

examples.note: it is necessary for him to believe

noteTranslations.es: es necesario que él crea
noteTranslations.fil: kailangang maniwala siya

examples.note: it is necessary for him to be baptized (passive infinitive)

noteTranslations.es: es necesario que él sea bautizado
noteTranslations.fil: kailangang mabautismuhan siya

sections.heading: 4. ὅστις — 'whoever'
sections.content: ὅστις (masc. sg.) / ἥτις (fem. sg.) / ὅ τι (neut. sg.) means 'whoever, anyone who.' It combines the relative pronoun with τις (someone). It refers to a class of people, not a specific individual, and takes an indicative verb when the statement is a general truth.

examples.greek: ὅστις μετανοεῖ καὶ πιστεύει, οὗτος λαμβάνει τὸ πνεῦμα
examples.note: whoever repents and believes, this one receives the Spirit

noteTranslations.es: quien se arrepienta y crea, éste recibe el Espíritu
noteTranslations.pl: ktokolwiek pokutuje i wierzy, ten otrzymuje Ducha
noteTranslations.fil: sinumang nagsisisi at naniniwala, siya ay tumatanggap ng Espiritu

examples.note: whoever is baptized, receives the gift

noteTranslations.es: quien es bautizado, recibe el don
noteTranslations.fil: sinumang nabautismuhan ay tumatanggap ng kaloob

sections.heading: 5. δίδωμι — present active forms
sections.content: δίδωμι ('I give') is a -μι verb — it follows a different conjugation pattern from regular -ω verbs. The stem is δο-/δι- and the endings are athematic (no thematic vowel before the ending). These forms appear frequently in this chapter.

examples.greek: ὁ πατὴρ δίδωσιν ἡμῖν τὸ πνεῦμα
examples.note: the Father gives us the Spirit (3rd sg.)

noteTranslations.es: el Padre nos da el Espíritu
noteTranslations.fil: ibinibigay ng Ama sa atin ang Espiritu

examples.note: we give you water (1st pl.)

noteTranslations.es: nosotros te damos agua
noteTranslations.fil: binibigyan ka namin ng tubig

examples.note: it is given by God (3rd sg. passive — note the passive form)

noteTranslations.es: es dado por Dios
noteTranslations.fil: ibinibigay ng Diyos

parts.label: Μέρος Βʹ — Τὸ Ἔργον τοῦ Πνεύματος καὶ ἡ Σάρξ

sections.heading: 1. κατά + accusative — 'according to'
sections.content: κατά with the accusative means 'according to,' 'in accordance with,' or 'along.' In Part B it appears in the key contrast περιπατεῖν κατὰ τὴν σάρκα / κατὰ τὸ πνεῦμα — to walk according to the flesh / according to the Spirit. This is the Pauline idiom for one's moral orientation or way of life.

examples.note: he walks according to the flesh (moral conduct governed by fleshly desires)

noteTranslations.es: camina según la carne
noteTranslations.fil: lumalakad ayon sa laman

examples.note: he walks according to the Spirit

noteTranslations.es: camina según el Espíritu
noteTranslations.fil: lumalakad ayon sa Espiritu

examples.greek: τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατός ἐστιν
examples.note: the mindset of the flesh is death (genitive of source/description)

noteTranslations.es: la mentalidad de la carne es muerte
noteTranslations.fil: ang isip ng laman ay kamatayan

sections.heading: 2. ἐάν + subjunctive — real conditional
sections.content: ἐάν ('if') introduces a conditional clause and is always followed by the subjunctive mood. This is called a third-class condition in Greek — it expresses a possible or likely future event. The main clause uses the indicative. The subjunctive form often looks like the present indicative but may have a slightly different vowel.

examples.greek: ἐὰν περιπατῶμεν τῷ πνεύματι, οὐ ποιοῦμεν τὰ τῆς σαρκός
examples.note: if we walk by the Spirit, we do not do the things of the flesh (ἐάν + subj.; main clause = indicative)

noteTranslations.es: si andamos en el Espíritu, no hacemos las cosas de la carne
noteTranslations.pl: jeśli kroczymy w Duchu, nie czynimy rzeczy ciała
noteTranslations.fil: kung lumalakad tayo sa Espiritu, hindi natin ginagawa ang mga bagay ng laman

examples.greek: ἐὰν ζῶμεν τῷ πνεύματι, καὶ τῷ πνεύματι στοιχῶμεν
examples.note: if we live by the Spirit, let us also walk in step with the Spirit

noteTranslations.es: si vivimos en el Espíritu, andemos también en el Espíritu
noteTranslations.pl: jeśli żyjemy Duchem, postępujmy też według Ducha
noteTranslations.fil: kung tayo ay nabubuhay sa Espiritu, lumakad din tayo ayon sa Espiritu

sections.heading: 3. ζάω — irregular contract verb 'to live'
sections.content: ζάω ('to live') is a contract verb whose stem ends in -α, but contracts unusually. The 3rd singular is ζῇ (not ζᾷ as expected) and the 1st plural is ζῶμεν. These forms appear directly in the story. The dative ζῶ τῷ πνεύματι means 'I live by/for the Spirit' — dative of means or instrument.

examples.greek: ὃς περιπατεῖ κατὰ τὸ πνεῦμα, οὗτος ζῇ
examples.note: the one who walks according to the Spirit, this one lives (3rd sg. ζῇ)

noteTranslations.es: el que camina según el Espíritu, éste vive
noteTranslations.pl: kto chodzi według Ducha, ten żyje
noteTranslations.fil: ang lumalakad ayon sa Espiritu, siya ay nabubuhay

examples.note: if we live by the Spirit (1st pl. subjunctive ζῶμεν; dative of instrument: τῷ πνεύματι)

noteTranslations.es: si vivimos en el Espíritu
noteTranslations.fil: kung tayo ay nabubuhay sa Espiritu

sections.heading: 4. The relative pronoun ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — 'who, which, that'
sections.content: The relative pronoun ὅς (masc.), ἥ (fem.), ὅ (neut.) introduces a relative clause and agrees with its antecedent in gender and number, but takes its case from its role within the clause. Part B uses it heavily — particularly ὅς (whoever walks…) and ὃ (which dwells in us…). The indefinite relative ὅς with a general antecedent often translates 'whoever.'

examples.greek: ὃς περιπατεῖ κατὰ τὸ πνεῦμα, οὗτος ἀγαπᾷ τὸν θεόν
examples.note: the one who walks according to the Spirit, this one loves God (ὅς agrees with the implied masc. subject)

noteTranslations.es: el que camina según el Espíritu, éste ama a Dios
noteTranslations.pl: kto chodzi według Ducha, ten miłuje Boga
noteTranslations.fil: ang lumalakad ayon sa Espiritu, siya ay nagmamahal sa Diyos

examples.greek: τὸ πνεῦμα, ὃ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν
examples.note: the Spirit, which dwells in us (ὅ is neut. agreeing with τὸ πνεῦμα; nominative in the relative clause)

noteTranslations.es: el Espíritu, que habita en nosotros
noteTranslations.fil: ang Espiritu, na nananahan sa atin

sections.heading: 5. The fruit of the Spirit — vocabulary
sections.content: Paul's list of the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22–23 appears in James's speech. Each noun is worth learning: ἀγάπη (love), χαρά (joy), εἰρήνη (peace), μακροθυμία (patience/longsuffering), χρηστότης (kindness), ἀγαθωσύνη (goodness), πίστις (faithfulness), πραΰτης (gentleness), ἐγκράτεια (self-control). Note that ὁ καρπός is singular — the Spirit bears one fruit with nine qualities.

examples.greek: ὁ καρπὸς τοῦ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἀγάπη καὶ χαρὰ καὶ εἰρήνη
examples.note: the fruit of the Spirit is love and joy and peace

noteTranslations.es: el fruto del Espíritu es amor, gozo y paz
noteTranslations.pl: owocem Ducha jest miłość, radość i pokój
noteTranslations.fil: ang bunga ng Espiritu ay pagmamahal, kagalakan, at kapayapaan

examples.greek: μακροθυμία καὶ χρηστότης καὶ ἀγαθωσύνη, πίστις καὶ πραΰτης καὶ ἐγκράτεια
examples.note: patience and kindness and goodness, faithfulness and gentleness and self-control

noteTranslations.es: paciencia, benignidad, bondad, fe, mansedumbre, templanza
noteTranslations.pl: cierpliwość, uprzejmość, dobroć, wierność, łagodność, powściągliwość
noteTranslations.fil: tiyaga, kabaitan, kabutihan, katapatan, kaamuan, pagpipigil sa sarili
